construction: Base W: replica heads at LBAs 19, 27 and 35 unreadable. ParityMap primary header at LBA 15 unreadable (medium error); tail header at LBA 16 intact. Footer at LBA 17 intact. No hints.

expected.path: no terminal replica validates (heads of A, B, C unreadable), so the Section 8.4.1 BOT walk runs; the bootstrap at file 0 reads, so no hints are needed
expected.outcome: BotStructuralRecoveryRequired, terminal authority not recovered; the walk completes and produces a 9-file map whose prefix (files 0-3) validates against the final ParityMap

1.class: Object candidate, identity unknown, 4 blocks, first ordinal 0

3.rung: item 4, tail route: head (LBA 15) unreadable, so the last block is read; the footer at LBA 17 has matching magic and parses; it locates the tail header at block 1 (LBA 16), which parses and agrees with the footer; footer total 3 = measured 3

4.rung: item 2, footer route (head unreadable, footer magic matches, footer parses, record count 3 = measured)

expected.validation_detail: The final ParityMap validates (footer valid, tail header valid and agrees, primary unreadable, is_final_directory true, directory nonempty). The second pass finds no Object candidate to reclassify (the sidecar is already a sidecar). The projection of files 0-3 hashes to canonical_map_digest; scope count 4 = ParityMap file number + 1; T = 4, W = 4. Validated scope is files 0-3. Files 4-8 are typed kind 4/5 in the measured tail, outside the validated scope.
expected.damage_reported_by_walk: No structural damage in the Section 12.2 sense (every file has one or more blocks and a filemark). No item 2 'damaged terminal replica' (footers parse, counts agree). Reported: terminal authority not recovered. Object identity unknown for file 1. The unreadable heads (ParityMap LBA 15; replica heads LBA 19, 27, 35) are findings a Verifier reports as unreadable components (Section 2.2); a Scanner's duty to report them is not stated (see notes).
sections_and_sentences: 12.3 'Unreadable head block: the Scanner MUST NOT abort. It MUST measure the file by filemark spacing, run the footer/tail sidecar probe, and otherwise classify the file as an object candidate. The last block it reads for that probe also serves the terminal footer probe of items 2 and 3. It also serves the tail route of item 4, and a file that item 4 recognises by that route is a ParityMap and not an object candidate.'

12.3 item 4: 'Away from tape file 0, when the first block is unreadable ... the walk reads the file's last block. If that block is a footer whose magic matches and that parses (Section 10.1.3), the footer locates the tail header copy at its tail_copy_start_block, and the file is a ParityMap if that tail header parses and agrees with the footer and the footer's parity_map_total_block_count equals the measured block count.'
12.3 item 2: 'When the head is unreadable, the file's last block is read, and a terminal footer whose magic matches establishes the same type, whether or not the footer parses.'

8.4 step 4 and 8.4.1: 'When A, B, and C are all absent or invalid, the Scanner MUST offer a full structural walk from BOT. The bootstrap supplies tape identity and geometry when it is readable.' and 'The Scanner MUST report that terminal authority was not recovered.'
12.4: 'If A, B, and C all fail, the Scanner returns an explicit BotStructuralRecoveryRequired outcome and performs the Section 8.4.1 walk'
10.1.3: 'When one header copy is invalid and the other is valid, the valid copy is used'; 10.1.5 and 13.1 for the validated final ParityMap, the second pass and the digest and scope checks

13.1: 'A map produced by the Section 8.4.1 walk, after the second pass of Section 12.3, is validated against the tape's final ParityMap when that ParityMap validates and is marked is_final_directory ... The validated scope and durable boundary are the first directory_scope_tape_file_count tape files, ending with that ParityMap's entry'
